_comment: The per-service baseline for a PROVIDER's docker-compose manifest — the other half
of the code root. brokerimages.json beside this one pins the guest OS a provider
boots (trust-chain hop 3); it says nothing about the containers inside, because
mr_config_id commits to the app-compose the OPERATOR chose. This file is what says
which containers we accept.
IT IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS A STATE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. An empty list means NOT
CONFIGURED: the comparison cannot run. Warn mode proceeds and says so; enforce
refuses every provider and names the unfinished configuration rather than blaming
the enclave. It never means 'accept anything'. The same contract osimages.json and
brokerimages.json have, for the same reason — a check that silently degrades to a
pass is worse than no check.
WHY IT IS STILL EMPTY. A baseline freezes a manifest, so the first entry decides
what we have accepted. cn-20's manifest today carries ten blocking findings from
the review (`pcverify -provider`, client/evidence/composereview.go): four images
pinned only by tag, `privileged: true` on prometheus-node-exporter along with
`/`, `/proc` and `/sys` mounts, and the container runtime's socket held by
0g-controller — which is OUR image. Recording that as the baseline would bless all
of it, and tightening afterwards is 'breaking compatibility' rather than a request.
So the first entries wait on the broker's next deployment, not on this mechanism.
HOW AN ENTRY IS WRITTEN, and why it holds TEXT. Run `pcverify -provider <addr>
-blocks` against the deployment. It prints, per service, the canonical block and —
labelled `no-image:` — the same block with the image identity held out. Copy the
one the rule below needs into `block`, one array element per line. Do not
hand-format it: both sides are reduced by evidence.CanonicalizeServiceBlock at
comparison time, so what is stored need not match the emitter byte for byte, but a
transcription error is still a transcription error.
Text rather than a digest, deliberately. A stored digest would bake the linked
gopkg.in/yaml.v3's formatting choices into this file, so a minor-version bump could
invalidate every entry at once and refuse every provider for a dependency upgrade.
Reducing both sides with one function at comparison time makes the library version
cancel out. And text is REVIEWABLE: a broker upgrade arrives as a legible diff
instead of a changed hash, which is the only way this file can be audited at all.
THE CANONICAL FORM IS NOT DEPLOYABLE YAML. Quoting is normalized away and the
image reference is replaced by `<image-held-out>`. It is a comparison form. Anything
that copies an entry into a compose file is misusing it.
THERE IS ONLY ONE IMAGE RULE, because the recorded block does the rest of the work.
`image` OMITTED — the default. Copy the `block` line from `-blocks` output. That
text contains the image line, so it pins the reference exactly as written: a
digest, a bare tag, or no image at all, whichever the deployment has. cn-20 runs
four services pinned only by tag, and this records them — because a baseline
answers 'is this the deployment we approved', not 'is this deployment good'. Those
are different questions, and the review keeps reporting the unpinned tag as a
blocking finding. Recording it here does not silence that.
"image": {"repository": "ghcr.io/..."} — any image in that repository, provided
it is pinned by digest. Copy the `no-image:` block instead, since the reference is
no longer pinned by the text. Use this ONLY where a release cadence would otherwise
force a gateway release per broker release: 0G's own broker image, which cn-20 runs
in three services. It accepts an older official build — a risk taken knowingly, to
be closed by a denylist later. And it always requires a digest: without one the
reference names a tag whose contents the registry can republish after the
measurement, so 'any image in our repository' would mean 'whatever is there now'.
There is deliberately no `digest` or `reference` rule. An earlier draft had both, and
writing the tests showed they could only restate what the block's image line already
says — while making it possible to record a block naming one digest and a rule naming
another, which would fail with a message about the wrong thing. A redundancy that can
disagree with itself is not documentation. Both keys are REJECTED rather than
ignored, so an author reaching for them is told what the format does instead.
WHAT A MATCH REQUIRES (evidence.CheckCompose): every service listed here present
exactly once, every service in the manifest listed here, each block equal after
reduction, and each image satisfying its rule. A service the baseline does not
mention is a MISMATCH, not an omission — an unlisted container is unreviewed code
inside the same guest, and 'ignore what we did not think of' is how a baseline
becomes decoration.
Fields: `name` is the compose service key. `block` is the canonical text, one array
element per line. `image` is the rule above.
